name: Legacy characterization test

problemSignals.description: The current behavior of a legacy path is not reliably known across representative inputs.
No executable observations protect the behavior that a change must preserve.
Unobserved side effects or failure semantics make modification likely to cause regressions.

requiredEvidence.description: Representative inputs, outputs, side effects, and failure semantics observed at the legacy entry point.
A repeatable command or harness that can execute the observations and retain their evidence.

assumptions: The legacy path can be invoked without changing its externally visible behavior
Observed examples are representative enough to define a bounded characterization contract

deterministicSteps.action: Select one legacy entry point and record its observable inputs, outputs, side effects, and failure surface.
Run the declared observation path for representative cases and capture exact results, side effects, and failures.
Encode the captured observations as a runnable characterization test without asserting unobserved implementation details.

outputs.description: Bounded contract of the legacy path's externally observable behavior.
Runnable regression check for the captured legacy behavior.
Evidence recording current outputs, side effects, and failure semantics.

whenAll: Representative inputs and failure cases are covered
Outputs and side effects are reproducibly captured
The characterization test passes from the runnable observation path
Core behavior is observed and runnable
Known long-tail inputs or side effects remain uncharacterized
The entry point or observation path cannot be executed

contraindications: No externally observable behavior can be captured
The observation path mutates production state without safe isolation
Examples would encode implementation details rather than behavior

contract: Invoke the bounded legacy entry point with declared fixtures
Capture outputs, side effects, and failures without changing behavior

inScope: Observable command, API, or library paths
outOfScope: Production execution without an isolated observation path
